analysis: Two changes were examined. (1) docs/threat-model.yaml adds one T-043 mitigation (head lines 1886-1892). It says the operator rollback (`darkbloom update --rollback`) uses the same journaled rollback, update lease, predecessor verification against the pinned designated requirement, and single-slot exact-version quarantine. It also says rollback refuses an installed bundle that differs from the recorded release and never rolls back one Mac of a cluster pair. This is documentation only, with no control weakened. It is consistent with T-043's existing limitations: rollback does not survive a reboot into a binary-level-broken candidate, quarantine is single-slot, and the bootstrap mitigation stays open. The claim is marked implemented, but the operator-rollback code path is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify it. That is a documentation-accuracy question, not a finding. (2) ProviderLoop+AutoUpdate.swift line 157 changes only the log text for the .quarantined outcome, from "after failed starts" to "on this Mac". Control flow, update lease handling, drain ownership, App Attest worker stop gating, and commit/restart logic (lines 84-344) are unchanged. The new message carries no sensitive data, since it only includes the version string. No regression in TB-011, T-043, T-053, or A-010 was identified. Remaining question for integration: confirm that the operator rollback implementation (outside this batch) matches the newly documented guarantees, namely the same update lease, designated-requirement verification, a differing-bundle refusal, and the cluster-pair guard. Nothing in this batch contradicts them.
